answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through slashable bonded staking. Nodes must lock capital into an escrow contract, establishing an onyx anchor of collateral forfeited upon cryptographic proof of misbehavior. This forces an attacker to dedicate scarce financial liquidity per identity, stopping an ocean of cheap clones from diluting consensus. While dynamic penalty thresholds flex like a willow under market volatility, the requirement excludes capital-poor agents.
